reasons: Sample lab values, findings and advice are shown when real data is missing, which can mislead a patient about their own health.
The trend chart uses fixed numbers, not the patient's history.
Loading errors are only logged to the console, so the user gets no message.
No tests are visible in this file.

terms.meaning: the patient's clear permission for the app to use AI on their data
running the document through the processing steps again, here after consent is given
optical character recognition, software that reads text from a scanned or photographed page
a number showing how sure the system is that it read the report correctly
held back, here meaning the AI summary is not shown until consent is given

used_by: Next.js route for a single report (apps/web/src/app/(dashboard)/reports/[id])

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the report page
sections.what: Brings in icons, navigation helpers, layout pieces, the two dashboard cards for summary and lab table, and the API helper.

sections.name: mockMarkers
sections.title: Built-in sample lab values
sections.what: Holds three sample results (hemoglobin, vitamin D, HbA1c), each with a value, range, status and plain explanation.
sections.why: Likely reason: used as placeholder content for demo and for reports with no real values.
sections.watch_out: These look like real results. Someone could mistake them for the user's own values, so they must not be shown for real reports.

sections.name: ReportSummaryPage (part 1)
sections.title: Loading the report and its summary
sections.what: When the page opens with a real report id, loads the document and its AI summary at the same time. Keeps whichever response arrives correctly and skips the demo ids. The summary, findings and advice then fall back to sample text when the real data is missing.
sections.why: Loading both together is faster, and one failure does not stop the other from showing. Reason the sample text is used as fallback is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Fallback text such as the named doctor and the vitamin D finding is shown when no summary is saved, so real patients can see advice that is not theirs.

sections.name: ReportSummaryPage (part 2)
sections.title: Lab value rows and the consent action
sections.what: Turns the real test results into table rows when they exist, otherwise uses the sample values. The consent handler saves consent, asks the backend to reprocess withheld documents, then reloads the report.
sections.why: Consent is required before AI reads the report, so the page needs one action to grant it and show the result.
sections.watch_out: If the consent save works but the reprocess fails, the error is only logged, and the user sees no clear message.

sections.name: ReportSummaryPage (part 3)
sections.title: Page header with report details
sections.what: Shows a back arrow, the document type, provider name, a short reference from the id, a Needs Consent tag when relevant, the report title, and PDF and Share buttons.
sections.why: Gives the user context on which report they are viewing.
sections.watch_out: The reference number is just the first eight characters of the id, not an official report number.

sections.name: ReportSummaryPage (part 4)
sections.title: Consent warning and main panels
sections.what: When the summary is withheld, shows an amber notice explaining the consent rule with a Grant Consent and Summarize button. Below it, shows the AI summary card and lab table on the left, and a side column on the right.
sections.why: The notice explains why the summary is missing and gives a direct way to fix it.
sections.watch_out: The notice refers to a specific law (DPDP Act). The wording is the app's own and should be checked by someone responsible for compliance.

sections.name: ReportSummaryPage (part 5)
sections.title: Trend bars and original source card
sections.what: Shows two small bar charts for hemoglobin and HbA1c with fixed numbers, a Full Trend View button, and a card for the original scan with a fixed date.
sections.why: Gives a quick visual sense of change over time. Reason the numbers are fixed is not stated in the code, so this appears to be a placeholder.
sections.watch_out: These bars do not reflect the patient's real history, so they must not be read as real trends.

summary: The detail page for one medical report, showing its title, AI summary, key findings, lab values table, and a consent prompt if the AI summary is held back.
purpose: Lets the user read one lab report in plain language and see its values, with an action to allow AI summarizing when consent is missing.
why: Reason not fully stated in the code. The page puts summary, values and source in one place so the user does not need to open the file.
how: On load it skips the fetch for the demo ids '1' and 'demo'. For real ids, it loads the document and its summary in parallel. Display falls back to built-in sample text and values when real data is missing. When the summary is withheld, the consent button records consent, asks the backend to reprocess, then reloads the report.
inputs: The report id from the page address, the document and summary data from the backend, and the consent button click.
outputs: A page showing the report title, the summary, key findings, recommendations, a lab values table, a confidence number, and a consent warning when relevant.
risks: The page falls back to sample lab values, sample findings and sample advice such as consulting a named doctor when real data is missing. A patient could read invented results as their own. The trend bars and source date are fixed in the code. The PDF, Share and View Scanned Image buttons have no action.
debug: If the wrong values appear, check whether the document response has an ocrResult with structuredData tests. If the values are sample ones, the backend data was not found or the id was demo or 1. If consent does not clear the warning, check the POST to /consents and the reprocess call, then the summary response.
